reason: The passage describes a profound covenant between Jonathan (a prince of elite status) and David (of humble origins), emphasizing their equal worth through deep personal bond. Jonathan voluntarily gifts David his royal garments and weapons, defends him against his father the king, and repeatedly proves his loyalty and affection transcend social hierarchy. The text repeatedly emphasizes they loved each other 'as [their own] soul' (כְּנַפְשׁוֹ), suggesting human worth and dignity that supersede social station. The narrative demonstrates neither that elite status confers inherent superiority nor that lower status implies inferiority—instead, it valorizes the mutual covenant and emotional connection between two people of unequal social position.
